p.src: Crimson gauze draped the walls; purple cords encircled the dais. Overhead hung a vermilion plaque; on every side descended curtains of mottled bamboo. The officials upheld justice; upon the admonition stone were carved four imperial lines. The clerks observed stern discipline; upon a lacquered tablet were written the two words “Speak Softly.” The commanding officers kept charge of confidential affairs; the reception office alone managed warrants and registers. The constables and soldiers stood grave and steady; the warders bore stern authority. Attendants gripping rattan switches stood before the steps; men bearing great cudgels left their ranks and divided to either side. When household, marriage, and civil suits were decided, the judgment shone as clearly as the jade balance of heaven. When quarrels, assaults, right, and wrong were judged, the verdict reflected all like a golden mirror. Though merely the chief magistrate of one prefecture, he was truly father and mother to the people from every quarter. Prisoners were made to stand as though upon ice, and all men to walk as though before a mirror; its manifold majesty defied description, like a whole hall of sculpted deities.

p.src: Grand Marshal Gao’s men brought Lin Chong before the court and forced him to kneel below the steps. They repeated the Grand Marshal’s words to Governor Teng and placed the sword that he had sealed before Lin Chong. The governor said, “Lin Chong, you are an instructor of the Imperial Guards. How could you be ignorant of the law and deliberately enter the Council Hall with a sharp blade in your hand? This is a capital offense.” Lin Chong pleaded, “Your Honor, whose judgment is a bright mirror, have mercy upon me, for I bear an unjust accusation. Though I am but a rough soldier, I know something of the law. How would I dare enter the Council Hall without leave? On the twenty-eighth day of last month, my wife and I went to the Temple of the Sacred Peak to redeem a vow. There we encountered Grand Marshal Gao’s young master, who molested my wife, and I shouted at him until he withdrew. Afterward he had Warden Lu lure me away to drink, while Fu An tricked my wife into going upstairs at Warden Lu’s house so the young master might molest her. Again I drove him off, and I caused an uproar at Warden Lu’s house. Though neither attempt at adultery succeeded, there are witnesses to both. The next day I bought this sword myself. Today the Grand Marshal sent two attendants to my home to summon me, telling me to bring the sword to his residence so it could be compared with another. Thus I accompanied the two men to the foot of the Council Hall. The two attendants went inside. Unexpectedly, the Grand Marshal then entered from outside, having laid this plot to frame me. I beg Your Honor to uphold justice for me.” After hearing Lin Chong’s deposition, the governor issued a written acknowledgment of receipt. Meanwhile, he had fetters and a cangue brought, placed Lin Chong in them, and committed him to prison. Lin Chong’s household came regularly to bring him food, all the while spending money on his behalf. His father-in-law, Instructor Zhang, also came, bribing those above and below and spending his wealth. Now the clerk in charge of the case was a man surnamed Sun and named Ding. He was exceptionally upright, delighted in doing good, and sought only to protect others; for this reason everyone called him Sun the Buddha. Knowing the truth of the matter, he spoke discreetly and circuitously throughout the prefectural offices, explaining its circumstances. Then he reported, “Lin Chong has indeed been wronged in this affair. We must find a way to save him.” The governor said, “He has committed so grave a crime! Grand Marshal Gao has endorsed the charge with the words ‘Let the crime be determined.’ He insists that Lin Chong be charged with deliberately entering the Council Hall, a sharp blade in hand, intending to murder him. How can we save the man?” Sun Ding said, “This Southern Court, the Kaifeng Prefecture, belongs not to the imperial court but to Grand Marshal Gao’s family.” “Nonsense!” said the governor. Sun Ding replied, “Who does not know that Grand Marshal Gao wields power and tyrannizes others by relying on his influence? Moreover, there is no wickedness his household will not commit. Whenever anyone gives him the slightest offense, he sends the person here to Kaifeng Prefecture. If he wants him killed, he is killed; if he wants him cut to pieces, he is cut to pieces. Does that not make this his family’s courthouse?” The governor said, “Then according to you, how can we accommodate Lin Chong and pass sentence upon him?” Sun Ding said, “Judging from Lin Chong’s deposition, he is an innocent man; the only difficulty is that we have no means of apprehending those two attendants. Have him confess merely that he improperly wore a sharp blade at his waist and mistakenly entered the Council Hall; then give him twenty strokes across the back and exile him to a remote and harsh military prefecture.” Governor Teng also understood the truth of the affair. He went in person before Grand Marshal Gao and repeatedly presented Lin Chong’s deposition. Gao Qiu knew in his heart that reason was against him, and he was reluctant to offend the governor, so he had no choice but to consent. That same day, the governor returned and convened the court. He had Lin Chong’s long cangue removed and sentenced him to twenty strokes across the back. He summoned a tattooer to mark Lin Chong’s cheeks and, according to the prescribed distance, assigned him to the prison fortress at Cangzhou. In the courtroom they fitted and nailed upon him a seven-and-a-half-catty round-headed iron-plated protective cangue, pasted the official seal upon it, issued an escort warrant, and assigned two constables to guard him on the journey.

p.src: The two men were Dong Chao and Xue Ba. Having received the official warrant, they escorted Lin Chong out of Kaifeng Prefecture. There they found all his neighbors and his father-in-law, Arms Instructor Zhang, waiting before the offices; together with Lin Chong and the two guards, they went to an inn beneath Zhou Bridge and sat down. Lin Chong said, “Thanks to Clerk Sun’s intervention, the beating was not severe, so I can still walk.” Arms Instructor Zhang told the innkeeper to prepare wine, food, and fruit for the two guards. After several cups had gone round, Arms Instructor Zhang produced some silver and gave it to the two escorting guards for their expenses. Taking his father-in-law by the hand, Lin Chong said, “Honored Father-in-law, ill fortune befell me this year and month: I crossed paths with Young Master Gao and was wrongfully prosecuted. Today I have something to submit to you: ever since you graciously favored me by giving me your daughter in marriage three years ago, there has never been the slightest fault between us. Though we have had no children, we have never once exchanged angry words or quarreled in the least. Now this calamity has overtaken me, and I am being exiled to Cangzhou, with no assurance whether I shall live or die. With my wife left at home, I cannot depart at ease, for I truly fear that Young Master Gao will use force to compel this marriage. Besides, she is still in the bloom of youth; she must not let Lin Chong ruin her future. This is Lin Chong’s own decision, made under no one else’s coercion. Today, in the presence of these good neighbors, I shall plainly write her a letter of divorce, leaving her free to remarry, and I shall raise no dispute whatever. Then Lin Chong can leave with an easy heart, and she may escape Young Master Gao’s persecution.” Arms Instructor Zhang said, “My worthy son-in-law, what are you saying! Your allotted years have merely fallen out of balance and calamity has struck you; this is not something you brought upon yourself. For now, go to Cangzhou and take refuge from this calamity. Sooner or later Heaven may show mercy and release you; when you return, husband and wife shall be reunited as before. This old man has enough at home to live on. I shall take my daughter and Jin’er back to my house, whatever may happen. For three years or five, I can provide for her. Nor shall I let her go abroad; even if Young Master Gao wants to see her, he will have no chance. Do not worry; leave everything to this old man. While you are in the prison fortress at Cangzhou, I shall frequently send you letters and clothing. Do not indulge in wild imaginings; set your mind at rest and go.” Lin Chong said, “I am grateful for your profound kindness, Honored Father-in-law. But Lin Chong cannot set his heart at rest; it would only delay us both in vain. Have pity on Lin Chong and grant my request; then I could close my eyes content even in death.” Arms Instructor Zhang would by no means consent. The neighbors also said it must not be done. Lin Chong said, “If you will not grant my request, then even should I struggle my way back, I swear I shall not live together with my wife again.” Arms Instructor Zhang said, “Since you insist upon it, write it for the time being as you wish. I simply shall not give my daughter to another man.” They immediately told the innkeeper to find someone who could draft documents and bought a sheet of paper. The man wrote as Lin Chong dictated:

p.src: Lin Chong, arms instructor to the eight hundred thousand Imperial Guards of the Eastern Capital, having been convicted of a grave crime and sentenced to exile in Cangzhou, cannot be assured whether he will live or die after his departure. As his wife, née Zhang, is still young, he willingly executes this letter of divorce, leaving her free to remarry, and shall never raise any dispute. This is indeed done of his own free will and not under compulsion. Lest there be no proof hereafter, this agreement is executed as evidence. Year, month, and day.

p.src: Just as the document was completed in the upper room and he was about to give it to his father-in-law for safekeeping, Lin Chong’s wife came running in, wailing to Heaven and earth. The maid Jin’er, carrying a bundle of clothes, had searched all the way to the inn with her. Seeing her, Lin Chong rose to receive her and said, “My wife, I have something to tell you, which I have already submitted to your father. Ill fortune befell Lin Chong this year and month, and I suffered this wrongful calamity. Now I am going to Cangzhou, with no assurance of life or death, and I truly fear I shall waste the flower of your youth. I have therefore written a few words here. I beg you not to wait for me; if a good opportunity presents itself, find another husband of your own accord, and do not let Lin Chong blight the future of his worthy wife.” When his wife heard this, she burst into tears and said, “Husband, I have never been stained by the slightest misconduct. Why do you divorce me?” Lin Chong said, “My wife, I mean it kindly. I fear that one day we shall only hinder each other and that I shall have cheated you of your life.” Arms Instructor Zhang then said, “Set your heart at rest, my child. Though your husband has decided upon this, how could I ever bring myself to marry you to another man? Let him leave with peace of mind for now. Even if he never returns, I shall provide the expenses for your whole lifetime; you need only remain faithful to him.” Hearing this, the woman choked with grief; then, seeing the letter, she suddenly fell to the ground weeping and lost consciousness. Before anyone knew the condition of her inward organs, they saw that her four limbs no longer moved. Indeed:

p.src: Jade from Mount Jing lies shattered—alas for the marriage bound by tressed hair through all these years; The flower before the precious mirror is withered—all in vain did the Lord of Spring spend ninety days in matching the pair. Her flowerlike face lies fallen, like a peony in the western garden leaning against a vermilion balustrade; Her sandalwood lips are silent, like Guanyin of the Southern Sea entering meditation. Last night an evil east wind swept the little garden, snapping the river plum and casting it prostrate on the ground.

p.src: Lin Chong and his father-in-law, Arms Instructor Zhang, managed to revive her. Only after a long while did she regain consciousness, and even then she could not cease weeping. Lin Chong gave the letter of divorce to Arms Instructor Zhang for safekeeping. Some women among the neighbors also came to console Lin Chong’s wife and supported her as they led her home. Arms Instructor Zhang exhorted Lin Chong, “Strive to make your way forward, and return so that we may meet again. Tomorrow I shall take your wife and household back with me and support them in my home until you return and the family is reunited. Go with an easy heart and do not worry. Whenever you find a trustworthy traveler, be sure to send letters frequently.” Lin Chong rose and thanked him, bowed farewell to his father-in-law and all the neighbors, shouldered his bundle, and departed with the guards. Arms Instructor Zhang and the neighbors took the road home; of that there is no more to tell.

p.src: Now the two escort officers brought Lin Chong to the constables’ quarters and placed him in custody, while Dong Chao and Xue Ba each went home to pack for the journey. As Dong Chao was tying up his bundles at home, a waiter from the tavern at the mouth of the lane came and said, “Officer Dong, a gentleman at our establishment wishes to speak with you.” “Who is he?” asked Dong Chao. The waiter replied, “I do not know him. He merely told me to ask you to come at once.” In the Song dynasty, constables were commonly addressed as “duangong.” Dong Chao immediately followed the waiter to a private room at the tavern. There he saw a man seated, wearing a swastika-patterned headscarf, a black gauze jacket, black boots, and clean socks. On seeing Dong Chao, the man hurriedly bowed and said, “Please be seated, Officer.” Dong Chao said, “I have never before had the honor of meeting you, sir. May I ask what service you require of me?” The man replied, “Sit down. You will know shortly.” Dong Chao sat opposite him. Meanwhile, the waiter laid out wine cups and filled the table with vegetables, fruit, and dishes to accompany the wine. The man asked, “Where does Officer Xue live?” Dong Chao replied, “In the lane just ahead.” The man summoned the waiter, asked for the exact address, and said, “Go and invite him here for me.” The waiter was gone for about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, then returned with Xue Ba to the private room. Dong Chao said, “This gentleman has invited us here to speak.” Xue Ba said, “Might I venture to ask your honorable name, sir?” The man again replied, “You will know presently. For now, please drink.” When the three had taken their seats, the waiter began pouring the wine. After several cups, the man drew ten taels of gold from his sleeve, set them on the table, and said, “You officers may take five taels apiece. I have a small matter with which I must trouble you.” The two said, “We have never met Your Honor before. Why would you give us gold?” The man said, “Are you two not bound for Cangzhou?” Dong Chao replied, “The prefectural office has ordered us to escort Lin Chong there under guard.” The man said, “Since that is so, I must ask a favor of you both. I am Lu, the security officer and trusted confidant of Grand Marshal Gao’s household.” Dong Chao and Xue Ba repeatedly murmured their assent and said, “Men of our lowly station would never dare sit at the same table with you.” Lu Qian said, “You both know that Lin Chong is the Grand Marshal’s enemy. I now act on the Grand Marshal’s command in bringing you these ten taels of gold. I trust you will accept the charge. There is no need to go far. At some secluded place ahead, finish Lin Chong off, obtain a written report there, and then return. Should the Kaifeng prefectural office raise any questions, the Grand Marshal will issue his own instructions, and no harm will come of it.” Dong Chao said, “I fear that cannot be done. The warrant from the Kaifeng prefectural office orders us to deliver him alive; it does not tell us to kill him. Besides, he is not yet advanced in years. How could we contrive such a thing? If any entanglement arose, it could prove most inconvenient.” Xue Ba said, “Old Dong, listen to me: if Grand Marshal Gao ordered us to die, we would still have no choice but to obey him. And here this gentleman is even giving us gold. Say no more. Let us divide it between us and do them this favor; then they may look after us in days to come. There are plenty of wild and perilous pine forests ahead. Somehow or other, we shall finish him off there.” Xue Ba thereupon took the gold and said, “Rest easy, sir. In five stages at most, perhaps as few as two days’ marches, the matter will be settled.” Lu Qian was delighted. “Officer Xue, you are indeed a forthright man! When the deed is done tomorrow, be sure to cut the branded mark from Lin Chong’s face and bring it back as proof. I, Lu Qian, will then guarantee another ten taels of gold in thanks to you both.

Dong Chao immediately followed the waiter to a private room at the tavern. There he saw a man seated, wearing a swastika-patterned headscarf, a black gauze jacket, black boots, and clean socks.
On seeing Dong Chao, the man hurriedly bowed and said, “Please be seated, Officer.”
Dong Chao said, “I have never before had the honor of meeting you, sir. May I ask what service you require of me?”
The man replied, “Sit down. You will know shortly.”
Dong Chao sat opposite him. Meanwhile, the waiter laid out wine cups and filled the table with vegetables, fruit, and dishes to accompany the wine.
The man asked, “Where does Officer Xue live?”
Dong Chao replied, “In the lane just ahead.”
The man summoned the waiter, asked for the exact address, and said, “Go and invite him here for me.”
The waiter was gone for about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, then returned with Xue Ba to the private room.
Dong Chao said, “This gentleman has invited us here to speak.”
Xue Ba said, “Might I venture to ask your honorable name, sir?”
The man again replied, “You will know presently. For now, please drink.”
When the three had taken their seats, the waiter began pouring the wine.
After several cups, the man drew ten taels of gold from his sleeve, set them on the table, and said, “You officers may take five taels apiece. I have a small matter with which I must trouble you.”
The two said, “We have never met Your Honor before. Why would you give us gold?”
The man said, “Are you two not bound for Cangzhou?”
Dong Chao replied, “The prefectural office has ordered us to escort Lin Chong there under guard.”
The man said, “Since that is so, I must ask a favor of you both.
I am Lu, the security officer and trusted confidant of Grand Marshal Gao’s household.”
Dong Chao and Xue Ba repeatedly murmured their assent and said, “Men of our lowly station would never dare sit at the same table with you.”
Lu Qian said, “You both know that Lin Chong is the Grand Marshal’s enemy.
I now act on the Grand Marshal’s command in bringing you these ten taels of gold.
I trust you will accept the charge.
There is no need to go far. At some secluded place ahead, finish Lin Chong off, obtain a written report there, and then return.
Should the Kaifeng prefectural office raise any questions, the Grand Marshal will issue his own instructions, and no harm will come of it.”
Dong Chao said, “I fear that cannot be done.
The warrant from the Kaifeng prefectural office orders us to deliver him alive; it does not tell us to kill him.
Besides, he is not yet advanced in years. How could we contrive such a thing?
If any entanglement arose, it could prove most inconvenient.”
Xue Ba said, “Old Dong, listen to me: if Grand Marshal Gao ordered us to die, we would still have no choice but to obey him.
And here this gentleman is even giving us gold.
Say no more. Let us divide it between us and do them this favor; then they may look after us in days to come.
There are plenty of wild and perilous pine forests ahead. Somehow or other, we shall finish him off there.”
Xue Ba thereupon took the gold and said, “Rest easy, sir. In five stages at most, perhaps as few as two days’ marches, the matter will be settled.”
Lu Qian was delighted. “Officer Xue, you are indeed a forthright man!
When the deed is done tomorrow, be sure to cut the branded mark from Lin Chong’s face and bring it back as proof. I, Lu Qian, will then guarantee another ten taels of gold in thanks to you both.

p.src: Dong Chao and Xue Ba divided the gold between themselves and took it home. Then they collected their luggage and bundles, picked up their constables’ staves, went to the quarters to fetch Lin Chong, and set out under orders to escort him. That day, after leaving the city, they traveled over thirty li before stopping to rest. In the Song dynasty, inns along the roads charged no lodging fee whenever constables escorting prisoners stopped there. Dong and Xue brought Lin Chong to an inn and spent the night there. At daybreak the next morning, they rose, lit the cooking fire, ate their meal, and took the road toward Cangzhou. It was the sixth month, and the summer heat was fierce. At first, after the beating, Lin Chong had not been much troubled. But after two or three days of blazing heat, the wounds from the cudgeling became inflamed. Since he had only recently been beaten, he could barely drag himself along the road, one step at a time. Xue Ba said, “What a witless fellow you are! Cangzhou lies more than two thousand li from here. If you walk like this, when will we ever arrive?” Lin Chong said, “I suffered some ill treatment at the Grand Marshal’s residence and was beaten only the other day. Now the wounds have flared up. In such scorching heat, I can only beg you both to bear with me, step by step.” Dong Chao said, “Walk slowly at your own pace. Pay no heed to his chatter.” All along the road, Xue Ba muttered, grumbled, and complained: “What cursed luck for us masters, to be saddled with a devil like you!” Before long, evening was again drawing in. And this is what could be seen:

p.src: The fiery wheel sank low, while the jade mirror was about to rise. In the distance, cooking fires rose from scattered cottages; nearby, brushwood gates stood half closed. Monks sought lodging in ancient temples, while crows could be glimpsed returning through the clouded woods; fishermen drew near the shadowed banks, while cicadas could still be heard crying among the windblown trees. Cattle and sheep hurried home from the heat, while weary donkeys and horses rested from the steaming road.

p.src: That evening, the three men found an inn in a village. Once inside their room, the two escorts laid down their staves and untied their bundles. Lin Chong also undid his bundle and, without waiting for the escorts to speak, took out some bits of silver. He asked the waiter to buy wine and meat and procure some rice, then had a meal prepared and invited the two escorts to sit down and eat. Dong Chao and Xue Ba ordered still more wine and plied Lin Chong until he was drunk and toppled over to one side, cangue and all. Xue Ba boiled a cauldron of water until it seethed, carried it in, poured it into a footbath, and called, “Instructor Lin, wash your feet before you sleep.” Lin Chong struggled to rise, but the cangue hampered him and he could not bend down. Xue Ba said, “I’ll wash them for you.” Lin Chong hurriedly replied, “You mustn’t.” Xue Ba said, “Men on the road can’t stand on so much ceremony.” Unaware that it was a trick, Lin Chong merely stretched out his feet. Xue Ba seized them and thrust them straight into the boiling water. Lin Chong cried out, “Aagh!” By the time he hastily snatched them out, the tops of his feet had been scalded red and swollen. Lin Chong said, “There was no need to trouble yourself.” Xue Ba said, “I have only ever seen convicts wait upon escorts; never have I seen escorts wait upon a convict. I kindly offered to wash his feet, yet he complains that the water is too cold or too hot. Truly, kindness gets no reward!” He muttered curses for half the night. Lin Chong dared not answer and lay down by himself to one side. The two men threw out that water, fetched fresh water for themselves, and went outside to wash their feet and make ready for bed. They slept until the fourth watch. Before anyone else at the inn had risen, Xue Ba got up, heated water for noodles, lit the fire, and prepared their meal. When Lin Chong rose, his head was reeling. He could neither eat nor walk. Xue Ba took up his fire-and-water staff and urged him to set out. Dong Chao untied from his waist a new pair of straw sandals whose loops and cords were woven of hemp, and told Lin Chong to put them on. Lin Chong looked and saw that his feet were covered all over with scald-blisters. He wished to find an old pair of sandals to wear, but where could any be had? With no other choice, he had to put on the new straw sandals. They had the waiter settle the wine bill, and the two escorts led Lin Chong out of the inn. It was then the fifth watch. Before Lin Chong had gone even two or three li, the new sandals had rubbed the blisters on his feet raw. Blood streamed from them; he could scarcely walk and groaned without cease. Xue Ba cursed him: “Walk, and walk quickly! If you won’t, I’ll drive you on with this great staff.” Lin Chong said, “Your Honors, please show mercy. How would this humble man dare to dawdle and delay the journey? The truth is that my feet hurt so badly I cannot walk.” Dong Chao said, “Then I’ll support you as you walk.” Holding Lin Chong up, he forced him to struggle onward another four or five li. Just as he was becoming utterly unable to walk, they saw ahead a savage-looking forest shrouded in smoke and locked in mist. Behold:

p.src: Layer upon layer, withered vines hang like trailing rain; luxuriant, towering boughs mass like banks of cloud. Who knows in what year the light of heaven last shone here? Only the wronged souls grieve without end.

Who knows in what year the light of heaven last shone here? Only the wronged souls grieve without end.

p.src: This forest was called Wild Boar Forest, the most perilous place on the road from the Eastern Capital to Cangzhou. In Song times, whenever anyone bore a grudge against another, he needed only give the escorts some money and have the man brought here. No one knew how many fine heroes had met their end in this forest. Now these two escorts led Lin Chong straight into this forest. Dong Chao said, “We have been walking the whole fifth watch and have not covered ten li. At this rate, how will we ever reach Cangzhou?” Xue Ba said, “I can walk no farther either. Let us rest awhile in the forest.”

In Song times, whenever anyone bore a grudge against another, he needed only give the escorts some money and have the man brought here. No one knew how many fine heroes had met their end in this forest.
Now these two escorts led Lin Chong straight into this forest.
Dong Chao said, “We have been walking the whole fifth watch and have not covered ten li. At this rate, how will we ever reach Cangzhou?”
Xue Ba said, “I can walk no farther either. Let us rest awhile in the forest.”

p.src: The three men went deep into the forest, took down their baggage and bundles, and set them all beside the roots of a tree. Lin Chong cried, “Aagh!” He leaned against a great tree and collapsed. Dong Chao and Xue Ba said, “Having to wait at every step has made us weary. Let us sleep awhile before going on.” They put down their fire-and-water staves and lay beside the tree. They had barely closed their eyes when they sprang up from the ground with a shout. Lin Chong asked, “Your Honors, what is the matter?” Dong Chao and Xue Ba said, “We want to sleep awhile, but there are no gates or locks here. We fear you may run away, and that worry keeps us from sleeping soundly.” Lin Chong answered, “This humble man is a man of honor. Since I have already submitted to the law, I would never flee as long as I live.” Xue Ba said, “How can we trust your word? If you want to set our minds at ease, we must tie you up.” Lin Chong said, “If Your Honors wish to tie me, then tie me. How would this humble man dare object?” Xue Ba untied a rope from his waist and bound Lin Chong tightly to the tree, hands, feet, cangue, and all. Then he and Dong Chao leapt to their feet, turned around, took up their fire-and-water staves, and said as they stared at Lin Chong, “It is not we who wish to finish you. When we came the other day, Officer Lu conveyed Grand Marshal Gao’s command: the two of us were to finish you here, take the branded seal as proof, and return at once to report. Even if you lived a few days longer, death would still be your fate. Better to do it here today—and help the two of us get back sooner. Do not blame the two of us. We act under orders from our superiors and have no choice in the matter. Mark this well: this day next year will be the anniversary of your death. We have been given a fixed deadline and must return early to report.” At these words, tears poured from Lin Chong like rain. He said, “Your Honors, I bore you no hatred in former days and hold no grievance against you now. If you two gentlemen can save this humble man, I shall never forget it, whether I live or die.” Dong Chao said, “What idle nonsense are you talking? We cannot save you!” Xue Ba raised his fire-and-water staff and brought it down toward Lin Chong’s head. Alas, the hero was bound hand and foot and could only await death. Truly: “Across ten thousand li of Yellow Springs there stands no inn; to whose house shall his three souls fall tonight?” As for whether Lin Chong survived, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
